clue.text: Figure mountain climbing, one occupying space

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the mountain word is read bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a net figure is a final sum after deductions, so figure can mean net

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is pictured as a lone figure hanging on the face of a peak, surrounded by empty air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like the definition but supplies NET; 'climbing' turns ALP upwards to PLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a heavenly body sitting in outer space, a cosmic occupant.

clue.text: Perhaps Emperor Nero finally supporting unity

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other one

parts.note: acting in concert means acting in unity

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word Nero

explanation.surface: It reads like a history note on the Roman emperor Nero backing a united empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Piano Concerto No 5 is nicknamed the Emperor; 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emperor is the popular title of a Beethoven piano work of this orchestral form.

clue.text: Loving wife to prepare for conflict

parts.note: to arm is to equip oneself for battle

explanation.surface: A tender spouse suddenly getting ready for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm person is affectionate, so loving and warm are synonyms.

clue.text: Order cider with one seen staggering around

indicators.note: staggering drunkenly about suggests the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral, and seen is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a pint of cider alongside a friend who has been spotted reeling about drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CIDER, I and SEEN gives the two words; 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi is a provisional court order in English divorce proceedings.

clue.text: American pro dropping ball is a big shock

indicators.note: the ball letter drops lower in the down entry, moving to the end of the word

parts.note: being pro something means being for it
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: A US sports professional fumbles the ball, which is a nasty surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' moves the O of FOR to the bottom, giving FRO. 'shock' is hair, not surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle, and a mass of thick hair is called a shock.

clue.text: Abuse alcohol with tear running

parts.note: malt is malt whisky, a type of alcohol

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are run about, put in a different order

explanation.surface: Drink-fuelled abuse ends with tears streaming down a face.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat someone is to treat them cruelly, a synonym of abuse as a verb.

clue.text: Flick cheese and soggy ground matter on back

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
a fen is low marshy land
to count is to matter, as in 'it counts'

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the word for on round

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: Instructions for a messy picnic: soft cheese, a boggy field and something squashed on someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses RE to ER. A flick is slang for a film; Brief Encounter is the 1945 British romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is a classic David Lean film, and flick is informal for a movie.

clue.text: Trade disc and record for sticker

parts.note: to sell is to trade goods
O is disc-shaped
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swaps records and discs to get a sticker in return.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellotape is a British brand of adhesive tape, so a sticker in the sense of something that sticks.

clue.text: Police leader seizes garment easy to lift for flashing

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so the leader's name wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: Sting was the frontman of the rock band The Police
a robe is a long garment
something light is easy to lift

explanation.surface: A senior police officer grabs a lightweight item of clothing during an indecent exposure arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police leader' suggests a chief constable, but means Sting, frontman of the band The Police; 'seizes' has his name wrapping the garment and the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobe lighting produces rapid bursts of bright light, flashing on and off.

clue.text: Pretty clothing line's pizzazz

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the word for pretty is wrapped around the other letter

parts.note: fair means attractive or pretty
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A smart fashion range has real panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is stylish originality, much like pizzazz or dash.

clue.text: Like Viking characters, hurry by a lot of rocks

parts.note: to run is to hurry

indicators.note: a lot of but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: Someone rushes past a heap of boulders, as Norse warriors might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ICE to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vikings wrote in runes, so their letters are runic.

clue.text: Top grade hiding a sign of infamy

indicators.note: to hide something is to put it inside, so the phrase wraps round the single letter

parts.note: the mark of the best is the top grade awarded

explanation.surface: A student's top mark conceals a dark secret.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into MARK OF THE BEST, making BEST into BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation the mark of the Beast brands followers of the Antichrist, so it is a stigma of evil.

clue.text: Defended only with locks

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
tressed means having tresses, locks of hair

explanation.surface: A castle was protected merely by bolts on its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests door fastenings but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttressed means supported or reinforced, so propped up against attack.

clue.text: Where one's picked up a blessing in disguise, right?

indicators.note: something in disguise has had its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A setback that turns out well, quizzically checking it's correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A BLESSING gives SINGLESBA. 'picked up' means chatted up.
explanation.definitionFit: A singles bar is a venue where unattached people go to meet and be chatted up.

clue.text: The first person to get cloned is an Internet hit

parts.note: me is the first person singular pronoun
a clone is an identical copy, so the first-person word is supplied again

explanation.surface: The world's first cloned human becomes a viral sensation online.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an image or idea copied and spread rapidly by web users.

clue.text: Dope in two varieties of blue

parts.note: the first of the two kinds of blue meant here is low, feeling depressed
the second kind of blue is down, also meaning sad

explanation.surface: Drugs come in two different shades of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from 'blue' in its sense of sad: LOW and DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside information, the same as the lowdown.

clue.text: Clean trousers in lake? It's a pain in the neck

definitions.text: It's a pain in the neck

indicators.note: to trouser something is to pocket it, so the washing word takes in the other pieces

parts.note: to wash is to clean
in means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: Washing trousers in a lake proves a tiresome chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplash is a neck injury from sudden jolting, literally a pain in the neck.

clue.text: Turn of phrase endlessly quoted, flipping silly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an idiom is a turn of phrase

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: cit. is the abbreviation for cited, meaning quoted

explanation.surface: An expression is repeated without end, a crazy thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts IDIOM to IDIO; 'flipping' turns CIT to TIC. 'flipping' also looks like a mild British intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means foolish or stupid, a synonym of silly.

clue.text: At home, fed entertaining young animal in brood

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so the letters hold the young animal

parts.note: in means at home
ate means fed, having eaten
a cub is a young fox, bear or lion

explanation.surface: A household where the family dines with a baby animal amongst its offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' seems a noun but is the verb, sitting on eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To incubate is to sit on eggs to hatch them, which is what a hen does when it broods.

clue.text: Strength of character essential to integrity

indicators.note: essential means at the heart, so the letters lie within the word

explanation.surface: Fortitude is a core part of honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, the toughness of a determined person.

clue.text: Desperately dry, I clam up in party

indicators.note: acting desperately suggests wild behaviour, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: At a celebration, someone parched and desperate goes silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid Cymru is a political party in Wales, a party in the political sense.

clue.text: Poor maiden before stealing silver

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: to steal is to take in, so the word for before wraps around the metal

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A penniless young woman, before committing a theft of silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or inadequate, a synonym of poor in quantity.

clue.text: Shows jeans with flower on the outside

indicators.note: the river word sits outside, around the jeans brand

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Tees in northern England
Levi's is a brand of jeans

explanation.surface: Denim trousers with a flower stitched on their exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: the Tees is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To televise is to broadcast on TV, so it shows programmes.

clue.text: Some force soldiers to desert rebellion

indicators.note: deserting means leaving, so the soldiers' letters are removed from the word

parts.note: a revolt is a rebellion
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A detachment of troops abandons an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The volt is the unit of electromotive force, so a measure of some force.

clue.text: Shot a bullet

explanation.surface: Firing off a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slug means both a gulp of spirits and a lump of metal fired from a gun.

clue.text: See 11
Alas, travelling after noon is congested, by the sound of it

definitions.text: congested, by the sound of it

indicators.note: after means the noon letter comes first
travelling means moving about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Bad news: a journey in the afternoon heat, and someone is all bunged up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal voice sounds as if spoken through a blocked nose.

clue.text: One who strays with no minor hesitations

parts.note: an adult is someone who is not a minor
er is a hesitation, and two of them are ERER

explanation.surface: A grown-up wanders off without the slightest pause.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer is unfaithful to a spouse, straying from the marriage.
